strategy_summary: For the first 7 rounds (below the model's 6-move history window) the AI played randomly, so I simply cycled through different moves to build a varied history rather than trying to exploit anything.

Once the LSTM started predicting (round 8+), the AI always plays COUNTER[predicted_move], so my core strategy was: read the displayed prediction and probabilities, infer the AI's actual upcoming move (the counter of its top prediction), and play the move that beats that.

This worked very well when the model was confidently locked onto one prediction (confidences up to 90-100%), producing long winning streaks, but the model adapted quickly once I repeated a move several times, flipping its prediction and punishing a stale strategy.

In the back half of the match probabilities often became close to uniform (35/33/31 or similar) or the model seemed to anticipate my reactive counter-play one step ahead, which produced a lot of ties in rounds 44-66 as our moves frequently coincided.

Overall the reactive counter-prediction strategy gave a solid edge over the AI (32 wins vs 22 losses), though the AI's adaptivity kept the game close and generated many ties rather than a one-sided result.
